screens.retrievalDescription: Desktop landing page hero section and social proof metrics for Fernway Learn. At the top, the navigation bar shows the purple 'Fernway Learn' brand logo, navigation links for 'Courses', 'Paths', 'Pricing', and 'Blog', alongside subtle right-aligned utility icon placeholders. The hero area uses a pale periwinkle gradient backdrop and a two-column layout. The left column presents the large bold headline 'Master AI skills that get you hired', featuring 'AI skills' highlighted in periwinkle font, followed by descriptive copy: 'Bite-sized courses, hands-on projects and an AI tutor that adapts to you. Join thousands of learners building real careers.' Underneath is a solid periwinkle CTA button labeled 'Get Started' beside a text link 'Learn more'. The right column displays an elevated, rounded card titled 'Your learning path' showing horizontal placeholder skeleton lines representing module progression. Positioned directly below the hero are four white stat cards highlighting '120+ Courses', '50k Learners', '4.8 Average rating', and '92% Completion', underlined by the credit line 'Trusted by teams at leading companies worldwide'.

Desktop pricing tier comparison page set against a plain white background. Centered text at the top reads 'Simple, transparent pricing' above the subhead 'Choose the plan that's right for you.' and a billing toggle reading 'Monthly · Yearly (save 20%)'. Below, three distinct plan cards are arranged horizontally. The 'Starter' tier card displays '$0/month', listing checkmarked features '5 intro courses', 'Community forum', and 'Certificates', paired with a light gray button labeled 'Submit'. The center 'Pro' tier card is highlighted with a violet border and a soft pink badge reading 'Popular'; it displays '$29/month' with features 'All 120+ courses', 'AI tutor', 'Projects with feedback', and 'Certificates', completed by a prominent purple button reading 'Get Started'. The rightmost 'Teams' tier card shows '$99/month' listing 'Everything in Pro', '10 seats', 'Admin dashboard', and 'SSO', alongside an outlined button labeled 'Contact us'. The screen utilizes clean modern typography with violet accents on the recommended option.

A clean, vertical account creation modal dialog displayed against a minimalist white background. The modal header features the brand name 'Fernway' in bold purple on the left and a gray close '✕' icon in the top right corner. The title block contains a bold primary header 'Create your account' supported by the subtitle 'Start learning in minutes.' Three rounded, outlined input fields follow in vertical succession with placeholder text: 'Full name', 'Email', and 'Password'. Below the inputs, an unchecked compliance box is paired with 'I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy'. A full-width, solid purple button labeled 'Submit' provides the main call to action. Beneath this, a subtle divider with the text 'or continue with' sits above three circular single sign-on buttons labeled 'G' for Google, 'in' for LinkedIn, and a command icon. At the bottom, secondary text prompts 'Already have an account? Log in'.

lead.summary: Fernway Learn presents a clean, modern aesthetic for its technical AI upskilling platform, featuring an organized landing page hero, clear pricing grid, and focused registration modal. However, the experience is severely hampered by widespread critical accessibility failures, including unreadable low-contrast hero copy (2.41:1), primary CTA text (1.95:1), and input placeholders (1.80:1). Usability is further compromised by generic 'Submit' action labels across free plan selection and account creation, floating inputs lacking persistent top labels, and a non-functional static billing frequency toggle. Addressing these foundational accessibility and UX defects will dramatically improve onboarding conversion and visual credibility against benchmarks like DataCamp and Codecademy.

fixes.action: Increase color contrast of the hero CTA button 'Get Started' to at least 4.5:1
fixes.why: The primary hero button text measures a critically low contrast of 1.95:1 (#f5ffff on #a5b4fd), making the core conversion entry point almost invisible to users with moderate visual impairments.

fixes.action: Add persistent text labels above input fields and boost border/text contrast in the sign-up modal
fixes.why: Inputs rely entirely on placeholder text measuring 1.80:1 to 1.82:1 with faint borders; placeholders disappear upon keystroke, degrading user memory, while screen readers and low-vision users lose form context.

fixes.action: Increase hero body copy contrast from 2.41:1 to meet WCAG AA 4.5:1
fixes.why: The value proposition copy '#9b9ead' against the lavender gradient '#f3f2fd' fails WCAG SC 1.4.3, significantly impairing readability for prospective learners.

fixes.action: Fix contrast and relabel the Starter plan button on the pricing screen
fixes.why: The button is ambiguously labeled 'Submit' and has a failing contrast ratio of 2.43:1 (#9f9ea2 on #f3f4f6). Changing it to 'Start for free' with dark text (#6f6e71 or darker) clarifies action intent and restores compliance.

fixes.action: Relabel the modal primary action from 'Submit' to 'Create account'
fixes.why: 'Submit' is a generic system technicality that fails to communicate the user outcome, violating usability and microcopy standards.

fixes.action: Implement an interactive billing duration toggle switch for Monthly vs. Yearly pricing
fixes.why: The text 'Monthly · Yearly (save 20%)' is displayed as static unsegmented text with no visual indication of which pricing mode is active, preventing users from exploring annual savings.

fixes.action: Replace hero skeleton placeholder card with authentic AI learning path content
fixes.why: The card visually anchors the hero with generic skeleton bars, failing to demonstrate the tangible product value, curriculum topics, or AI tutor capabilities.

fixes.action: Increase touch target size and accessible label for modal close icon
fixes.why: The modal close button measures only 11×14 CSS px (violating WCAG 2.5.8 target size minimum of 24×24 CSS px) and measures 2.67:1 contrast without an explicit screen-reader label.

fixes.action: Fix contrast and enlarge click target for 'Log in' secondary link
fixes.why: The modal login link has a critically low contrast ratio of 2.12:1 (#a9b0d0 on #fdfdfe) and a height of only 14 CSS px, causing friction for returning learners attempting to authenticate.

fixes.action: Enlarge checkbox touch target and increase contrast on terms agreement
fixes.why: The sign-up checkbox measures only 14×14 CSS px and registers 1.52:1 contrast against the modal canvas, creating input frustration and failing WCAG SC 2.5.8 and 1.4.3.

fixes.action: Replace ambiguous command glyph ('⌘') SSO icon with a recognizable provider logo
fixes.why: The third SSO provider button uses a keyboard command symbol instead of a standard third-party identity provider logo like Apple or GitHub, confusing prospective users.

fixes.action: Adjust top navigation links to meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) and target size (24px)
fixes.why: Links ('Courses' 4.25:1, 'Paths' 4.44:1, 'Pricing' 3.87:1, 'Blog' 3.90:1) fail the 4.5:1 text contrast threshold and possess vertical touch heights of only ~13 CSS px.

fixes.action: Darken the social proof line 'Trusted by teams at leading companies worldwide'
fixes.why: The trust banner text uses faint gray typography below WCAG AA thresholds, diminishing the intended credibility boost for enterprise buyers.

fixes.action: Adjust 'Learn more' link contrast and tap target padding in hero
fixes.why: 'Learn more' link contrast measures 4.08:1 against the gradient background and has a target height of only 15 CSS px, falling short of target size standards.

fixes.action: Normalize headline typography color for 'AI skills'
fixes.why: Highlighting 'AI skills' with an isolated purple hue is an overused template styling pattern; using uniform typography weight and scale improves visual craftsmanship.

Replace the ambiguous '⌘' SSO symbol with an official GitHub or Apple provider icon

visual.title: Visual hierarchy
visual.text: Size, weight, colour, contrast and position tell users what to look at first. One primary action per view should be visually dominant; secondary actions recede. Competing accents dilute focus.

visual.title: Form design
visual.text: Use single-column forms with labels above fields, group related fields, mark optional rather than required fields where most are required, use input types that match the data, and keep the primary button label specific to the outcome.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
a11y.text: Visual information needed to identify user interface components and states, such as icon buttons, input borders, focus indicators and chart elements, needs at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 2.5.3 and 4.1.2 Labels and names
a11y.text: Inputs need visible labels that stay visible while typing; placeholders are not labels. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. The visible label text should be part of the accessible name.
